subject: [PATCH] mm: page_alloc: make defrag_mode retries follow the promoted order

reviews.author: Harry Yoo
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Harry Yoo suggested that the patch should distinguish between order and compact/reclaim_order in __alloc_pages_slowpath() to improve code readability and prevent mistakes.

Reviewer Harry Yoo questioned the logic of changing how hard direct compaction tries to compact in defrag_mode, suggesting it doesn't align with the rest of the patch
reviews.raw_body:
I think we should start distinguishing order and compact/reclaim_order
in __alloc_pages_slowpath(). Silently overriding it makes it harder to
follow and easy to make a mistake.

---

This would change how hard we try to compact with defrag_mode in direct
compaction as it won't try compaction with MIN_COMPACT_PRIORITY anymore.

It doesn't make much sense to change that as part of this fix?

2026-09-29.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of page allocation in defrag_mode to make retries follow the promoted order, rather than the original request order. This change is intended to prevent indefinite retrying by requests that are not movable, which can lead to reclaim storms and excessive memory pressure. The patch treats promoted requests as costly orders, resetting progress counters for them and checking compaction results at the promoted order. It also resets retry counters when a fallback attempt is taken, allowing it to get a full retry budget before the OOM killer is considered. This change aims to improve performance and reduce memory pressure in systems with high inode churn under memory.low protection.
